The package is small and readable, and the existing tests pass after installing declared deps (`9 passed`). I would not approve it as-is: the main concerns are unescaped path parameters, no retry/wrapping for transport failures, unsafe retry semantics for POSTs, weak runtime validation, and mutable internals in “frozen” models.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: about 170 LOC, including production fixes and focused tests. `compileall` could not run meaningfully because `/work` rejects `__pycache__` writes.

issues.description: Transport errors from httpx are not retried or wrapped, so transient network failures leak raw exceptions after one attempt.
Retry logic can replay non-idempotent POST requests after server errors without idempotency keys or method-aware safeguards.
Path parameters are interpolated without URL escaping, allowing slash/query injection into request URLs.
Retry-After only supports numeric seconds and ignores valid HTTP-date header values.
Pagination has no repeated-cursor guard or cursor type validation, so malformed responses can cause infinite loops.
Malformed list items are silently skipped instead of raising a schema/API error.
Constructor accepts invalid max_attempts values, which can make requests fail before being attempted.
review() relies on static Literal typing only and sends invalid runtime verdict strings unchecked.
Literal enum fields from API responses are not runtime validated, so invalid states/statuses are accepted.
Frozen dataclasses retain and return mutable dict references, so model state can be mutated externally.
Malformed API payloads raise raw KeyError/TypeError/ValueError instead of a client-level schema error with context.
Tests cover happy paths and selected API errors but miss transport failures, URL escaping, malformed schemas, and runtime enum validation.
